record.paper_title: Ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms: some open problems
record.original_question: Arendt, [ 2 , 3 ], has given an indirect proof using deep results of Brainerd and Edwards that if G is a locally compact group then the left regular representation of \(L^1(G)\) in \({\mathcal L}^r\big (L^1(G)\big )\) is a lattice homomorphism. He also proves that if \(1<p<\infty \) and G is amenable then the action of \(L^1(G)\) on \(L^p(G)\) gives a lattice homomorphism of \(L^1(G)\) into \({\mathcal L}^r\big (L^p(G)\big )\) . Give a direct proof.

evidence.quote: Arendt, [ 2 , 3 ], has given an indirect proof using deep results of Brainerd and Edwards that if G is a locally compact group then the left regular representation of \(L^1(G)\) in \({\mathcal L}^r\big (L^1(G)\big )\) is a lattice homomorphism. He also proves that if \(1<p<\infty \) and G is amenable then the action of \(L^1(G)\) on \(L^p(G)\) gives a lattice homomorphism of \(L^1(G)\) into \({\mathcal L}^r\big (L^p(G)\big )\) . Give a direct proof.
Update: This has been solved in [ 11 ], where the amenability condition on G in the case \(1<p<\infty \) is removed. This is ongoing research and will be published in due course.

artifact.category_tag: Banach lattice representations of group algebras
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a locally compact group with a fixed left Haar measure, and let $L^1(G)$ denote the group algebra of $G$, viewed as a complex Banach lattice under pointwise (a.e.) ordering. For a Banach lattice $E$, let $\mathcal{L}^r(E)$ denote the Banach lattice of regular (i.e., differences of positive) bounded linear operators on $E$, equipped with the regular operator norm and the natural ordering.

(a) Give a direct proof (not relying on the deep convolution-operator results of Brainerd–Edwards) that the left regular representation
$$\lambda : L^1(G) \longrightarrow \mathcal{L}^r\bigl(L^1(G)\bigr), \qquad \lambda(f)g = f * g,$$
is a lattice homomorphism, i.e., $\lambda(|f|) = |\lambda(f)|$ in $\mathcal{L}^r(L^1(G))$ for every $f \in L^1(G)$.

(b) For $1 < p < \infty$, give a direct proof that the natural action
$$\pi_p : L^1(G) \longrightarrow \mathcal{L}^r\bigl(L^p(G)\bigr), \qquad \pi_p(f)\xi = f * \xi,$$
is a lattice homomorphism. (Determine in particular whether the amenability hypothesis on $G$ is necessary.)
artifact.status_search_result: According to the problem's own update note, the question has been resolved: a direct proof has been given, and in the $1<p<\infty$ case the amenability assumption on $G$ has been removed. The result was announced as forthcoming publication.
